+            LC_ALL=C sort aur/.SRCINFO > /tmp/camcraft.expected.srcinfo

+            diff -u /tmp/camcraft.expected.srcinfo /tmp/camcraft.actual.srcinfo

       - name: Build and test Arch package

       - name: Check package contents

-          bsdtar -tf aur/camcraft-*.pkg.tar.zst | grep -E '(^|/)usr/lib/camcraft/camcraft-ui$'
-          bsdtar -tf aur/camcraft-*.pkg.tar.zst | grep -E '(^|/)usr/share/applications/camcraft.desktop$'
+          set -- aur/camcraft-[0-9]*.pkg.tar.zst
+          [ "$#" -eq 1 ] && [ -f "$1" ]
+          bsdtar -tf "$1" | grep -E '(^|/)usr/lib/camcraft/camcraft-ui$'
+          bsdtar -tf "$1" | grep -E '(^|/)usr/share/applications/camcraft.desktop$'
+          mkdir -p dist
+          cp "$1" dist/
       - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4

-          path: aur/camcraft-*.pkg.tar.zst
+          path: dist/*.pkg.tar.zst

@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+## #72 - AUR, FreeBSD and WebAssembly build targets (2026-11-08)
+
+- **Chosen:** keep the AUR source recipe pinned to the latest published tag,
+  v0.14.0, with a checked source archive hash. Compare normalized `.SRCINFO`
+  fields in the Arch workflow: the earlier run failed only because makepkg
+  moved `options = !lto` after the dependencies. The Arch job follows Linux
+  in `release.yml`; on a tag it downloads that tag's archive, checks its
+  SHA-256, and builds a matching package even before the tracked AUR recipe
+  receives its next version update.
+- **Chosen:** build FreeBSD amd64 natively in a FreeBSD 14 VM and package the
+  three executables with adjacent assets in a tarball. Manual and tagged
+  release runs produce the archive. A native VM supplies
+  FreeBSD libc and system libraries, which a Linux build cannot provide.
+- **Chosen:** leave Web/WASM untouched until issue #31 completes its browser
+  UI port. Its existing domain build remains in the manual CI workflow.
+- **Dropped:** publishing the AUR recipe automatically before the Arch build
+  is validated and an AUR maintainer is configured; calling a linked WASM
+  CLI a browser UI; treating a Linux binary as a FreeBSD release.
+- **Cost to change:** low for the package and workflow wiring. A runnable
+  browser UI is a separate application port, not a packaging change.

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Package native FreeBSD binaries with assets adjacent to the executables.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+root=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
+cd "$root"
+
+if [[ $(uname -s) != FreeBSD || $(uname -m) != amd64 ]]; then
+    echo "package-freebsd: this script packages FreeBSD amd64 binaries" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+bin_dir=${CAMCRAFT_BIN_DIR:-target/release}
+dist=${CAMCRAFT_DIST_DIR:-dist}
+for binary in camcraft-ui camcraft-cli post; do
+    if [[ ! -x "$bin_dir/$binary" ]]; then
+        echo "package-freebsd: missing executable $bin_dir/$binary" >&2
+        exit 1
+    fi
+done
+version=$("$bin_dir/post" --version | awk '{print $2}')
+if [[ ! $version =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
+    echo "package-freebsd: unexpected post version '$version'" >&2
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+mkdir -p "$dist"
+dist=$(cd "$dist" && pwd)
+name="camcraft-$version-freebsd-amd64"
+work=$(mktemp -d "$dist/.package-freebsd.XXXXXX")
+trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
+stage="$work/$name"
+mkdir -p "$stage/assets"
+
+for binary in camcraft-ui camcraft-cli post; do
+    install -m 755 "$bin_dir/$binary" "$stage/$binary"
+done
+for asset in posts machines ui scripts themes; do
+    cp -R "assets/$asset" "$stage/assets/$asset"
+done
+install -m 644 RELEASE_NOTES.md TESTING.md LICENSE README.md "$stage/"
+tar -C "$work" -czf "$dist/$name.tar.gz" "$name"
+echo "FreeBSD package: $dist/$name.tar.gz"
